entries.readme_excerpt: I built Person Presence because I wanted a more realistic answer to a fairly simple question: where is everyone? In my case, I use it to help show people's actual location on my Home Assistant dashboards, whether they are at home or out and about. At home, I'd like to know which room they are in. Away from home, I'd like to show the zone they are in, or just that they are away if that is all the available information can tell me. The bit I wanted to try and fix was the difference between knowing where someone's devices are and knowing where the person is. A phone, watch and iPad can all belong

entries.description: Water Boiler sync with radiator valves for Meross devices
entries.readme_excerpt: Meross Boiler Sync is a custom Home Assistant integration designed to bridge the gap between Meross smart radiator valves and independent room thermometers/hygrometers. In the native Meross ecosystem, heating demand and temperature regulation are controlled exclusively by the built-in sensors located directly inside the valves right next to the hot radiator. This often causes valves to shut off prematurely because radiant heat tricks the sensor while the rest of the room is still cold. This integration solves that problem by delegating heating demand calculations to external room thermometers

entries.title: Adds new integration [Semir333/meross_boiler_sync]
entries.description: Water Boiler sync with radiator valves for Meross devices
entries.readme_excerpt: Meross Boiler Sync is a custom Home Assistant integration designed to bridge the gap between Meross smart radiator valves and independent room thermometers/hygrometers. In the native Meross ecosystem, heating demand and temperature regulation are controlled exclusively by the built-in sensors located directly inside the valves right next to the hot radiator. This often causes valves to shut off prematurely because radiant heat tricks the sensor while the rest of the room is still cold. This integration solves that problem by delegating heating demand calculations to external room thermometers

entries.readme_excerpt: A Home Assistant helper that groups Z-Wave JS covers, lights, switches or fans into one entity and commands them with a single Z-Wave multicast frame, so they act at the same A normal group calls each member separately. The Z-Wave controller then sends one acknowledged frame per device, waiting for each acknowledgement before the next, so the members start about a second apart. On a pair of roller shades, or a row of lights, Home Assistant doesn't multicast group calls yet (see feature-requests #3976 and Until it does, this helper gives you a group entity that does. entries.description: Water Boiler sync with radiator valves for Meross devices
entries.readme_excerpt: Meross Boiler Sync is a custom Home Assistant integration designed to bridge the gap between Meross smart radiator valves and independent room thermometers/hygrometers. In the native Meross ecosystem, heating demand and temperature regulation are controlled exclusively by the built-in sensors located directly inside the valves right next to the hot radiator. This often causes valves to shut off prematurely because radiant heat tricks the sensor while the rest of the room is still cold. This integration solves that problem by delegating heating demand calculations to external room thermometers

There it cools down, its relative humidity rises, and water condenses on the cold walls. Ventilating makes the basement wetter instead of drier. entries.readme_excerpt: ℹ️ Junges Projekt. Version 0.1 ist die erste Version zum Testen. Rückmeldungen sind sehr willkommen – siehe Fehler melden. Eilwacht bringt Eilmeldungen und Regionalnachrichten der Tagesschau in dein Home Assistant – nicht als Nachrichtenleser, sondern als Auslöser: für eine Push-Nachricht, eine Ansage in der Küche oder ein Lichtsignal. Nachrichtenwächter melden dir neue Meldungen aus deinem Bundesland, auf Wunsch nur die mit bestimmten Stichworten wie „Warnstreik“ oder „S-Bahn“. entries.title: Adds new integration [ajachierno/Lego-Power]
entries.description: Home Assistant integration to control LEGO Powered Up motors over Bluetooth
entries.readme_excerpt: A Home Assistant integration that controls LEGO® Powered Up motors directly over Bluetooth Low Energy, using the LEGO Wireless Protocol v3. Each LEGO hub becomes a proper Home Assistant device with controllable entities, so you can run and stop motors from the UI, dashboards, scripts and automations — no helper scripts or button presses required. The integration supports multiple hubs, each added as its own device. LEGO® is a trademark of the LEGO Group, which does not sponsor, authorise or Tested only on the LEGO® Piano (21323). Other Powered Up hubs and motors should work, but are unverified
entries.name: LEGO Power

entries.description: Home Assistant integration: keep Alexa groups in sync with your Home Assistant areas and floors. Uses the Alexa Devices or Alexa Media Player sign-in. Dry-run by default.
entries.readme_excerpt: Keep your Alexa groups in step with your Home Assistant areas, so "Alexa, turn off the kitchen" controls what HA calls the kitchen. HA Cloud exposes your devices to Alexa but can't create groups. This creates one for each area and keeps it up to date, with optional groups per floor. ⚠️ This uses Amazon's undocumented Alexa API, which can change without notice. It previews by default and writes nothing until you turn writes on. Home Assistant 2025.12 or later. A signed-in Alexa account in either integration. entries.title: Adds new integration [EndOfTheLine-HA/ha-website-health]
entries.description: Is it down, or is it me? Home Assistant integration that checks your website really works (required text, JSON keys) and tells a site outage from your own internet outage. HACS custom integration.
entries.readme_excerpt: Website Health for Home Assistant Website Health checks that a website really works, not just that it answers. On a schedule it fetches the pages and files you list, confirms each one returns success and contains the text (or JSON keys) you say it must, and turns the result into When checks fail, it first asks two unrelated hosts whether your own internet works. If they cannot be reached either, the status reads My internet is down instead of Down, so an outage at home is never reported as your site being down. UI configuration; no YAML. One entry per website, with as many checks as you like.

entries.title: Adds new integration [bionic-tech/ha-cluster-state-sync]
entries.description: Alpha. Active-passive failover for Home Assistant: mirrors state and configuration to a standby and restores it before automations run. Both nodes fire automations during the overlap, and a promoted standby has no radios.
entries.readme_excerpt: Active-passive failover for Home Assistant. It mirrors entity state and configuration into a shared Valkey or Redis, and restores them on the standby at startup, before the automation engine runs, so a freshly promoted node does not act on empty or stale state. Measured on real hardware: a standby fully initialised in ~102 seconds after host loss. That number covers losing the whole machine, and the promoted node had no radios attached. Home Assistant failing on its own is slower on purpose. ⚠ Alpha — read this before installing No guarantees are given on data integrity or on consistency of fu

entries.description: Home Assistant integration for KOSTAL KSEM: local WebSocket/Protobuf push, UI setup, six phase sensors, no Modbus TCP
entries.readme_excerpt: KOSTAL KSEM WebSocket · v0.1.1 Inoffizielle Home-Assistant-Custom-Integration für den KOSTAL Smart Energy Meter. Einrichtung über Einstellungen → Geräte & Dienste → Integration hinzufügen → KOSTAL KSEM WebSocket mit IP/Hostname und Administratorpasswort. Local Push über WebSocket/Protobuf. Kein Modbus TCP, kein KSEM TCP-Slave. Die Integration aktiviert keine Geräteschnittstellen und schreibt keine KSEM-Einstellungen. entries.description: Local Home Assistant integration for NIBE heat pumps and indoor modules, without the cloud: S-series over Modbus TCP, F-series through a NibeGW gateway. Finds which registers your unit actually has and explains each one in plain language.
entries.readme_excerpt: Local communication between Home Assistant and NIBE heat pumps and indoor modules. No cloud, no myUplink account. The S-series has Modbus TCP built in, so it needs no extra hardware. The F-series, which has no Modbus TCP, is reached through a NibeGW gateway on the pump's RS-485 bus, built with Nibe F-series ModbusAdapter. It differs from the existing options in two ways, both of which came out of actually probing a pump rather than reading the documentation: 1. It finds out which registers your pump really has. entries.title: Adds new integration [adamg23/Eufy-Omni]
entries.description: Home Assistant integration for Eufy Omni robot vacuums (C28, X10 Pro Omni) over the Eufy Clean cloud
entries.readme_excerpt: Eufy Omni C28 for Home Assistant A from-scratch Home Assistant integration for Eufy Clean "Omni" robot vacuums (tested on the Omni C28 T211A and X10 Pro Omni T2351). Talks to the Eufy Clean cloud the way the app does: HTTPS login, then a mutual-TLS MQTT connection that pushes the robot's state as protobuf-encoded data points. No polling in normal operation. eufyomnicloud/ – standalone async client (aiohttp + paho-mqtt + protobuf). customcomponents/eufyomni/ – the integration: vacuum, sensors, binary sensors, buttons, selects, volume, a map camera, services eufyomni.startscene / eufyomni.startr

entries.title: Adds new integration [Dinnsen/EV-Guest]
entries.description: EV Guest for Home Assistant helps you find the cheapest charging window for guest EVs without connecting the car to Home Assistant.
entries.readme_excerpt: EV Guest for Home Assistant A guest arrives with an electric car and leaves in the morning. EV Guest finds the cheapest hours to charge it from your electricity prices – without adding the car to Home Assistant. Enter the license plate, say how full the battery is and when the car must be ready, and EV Guest plans the charging, shows what it costs and what you save, and starts and pauses your charger exactly when the plan says – then hands it back when the guest has gone. EV Guest is a calculator: it never switches a charger itself. A two-line automation or EV Smart Charging does the charging.
entries.name: EV Guest

entries.title: Adds new integration [virtumaps/virtuhome]
entries.description: Your home as a live 3D model in Home Assistant
entries.readme_excerpt: Your home as a live 3D model in Home Assistant. Lights glow in their real colours and light up their rooms, doors swing with their contact sensors, blinds follow their covers, cameras, motion and alarms show where they are, and walls between you and a room slide out of the way. Try the online demo: turn the house, switch the lights and open the editor in your browser, no Home Assistant needed. Built for wall tablets first: on a Fire HD 8 class tablet the view draws nothing while nothing changes, each floor is one or two draw calls, and lighting is computed on the CPU only when a light changes.
entries.name: VirtuHome

entries.readme_excerpt: Taryfy energii PL dla Home Assistant Cena prądu brutto za każdą godzinę: energia (stała z cennika albo dynamiczna z giełdy) plus dystrybucja według grupy taryfowej. entries.title: Adds new integration [WOOWTECH/Woow_ha_serial]
entries.description: WOOW Serial: RS485 / RS232 devices as native Home Assistant devices. Monitor and learn frames, build entities, keypad triggers, all from a sidebar admin panel. HACS custom integration (繁體中文 / English).
entries.readme_excerpt: 把 RS485／RS232 設備變成 Home Assistant 的原生裝置：在側邊欄面板監看線路上的訊框、學起來、組成裝置和實體，牆面按鍵也能直接觸發自動化。不需要寫 YAML。 管理面板的做法參考 HAIR（Home Assistant 紅外線管理面板）。 本機串口：Raspberry Pi 上的 RS485（SC16IS752，/dev/ttySC）和 RS232（/dev/ttyAMA0）。 外接設備：綁定其他整合提供的串口，例如渥屋 HA-WF485-V3（ESPHome）。選了裝置就會自動帶入要用的實體。 自動辨識 9 種校驗碼（CRC16/Modbus、CRC16/CCITT、SUM8、XOR8 等）。 把指令組成窗簾、燈光、開關、影音設備、選擇器，自動產生 cover／light／switch／mediaplayer／select 實體，每個指令另有一個按鈕。 解析設備的回覆來更新狀態，也可以讀出感測數值、定時輪詢。 牆面按鍵（或任何會主動送訊框的輸入設備）的每個鍵都可以觸發自動化。在自動化編輯器裡直接選「裝置 → 按下某鍵」，按鍵改名也不會讓舊的自動化失效。 記錄 HA 送出的每一筆，以及是誰送的（服務、實體、面板、裝置），還有對方有沒有回覆、回覆花了幾毫秒。 同一條線上的其他埠如果也收到，就證明真的送上了線。這種回音不會進監看，也不會觸發按鍵。 內建範本庫：杜

entries.readme_excerpt: The Home Assistant dashboard for the screen on the wall. Home Assistant can run the whole house. Most of the people in it just want the lights, the heating, the music and the front door, and they want those to be obvious. HouseView is that screen: a few pages you can swipe, with controls big enough to hit on the first try. It is opinionated about what goes on the page. A light is a button you hold to dim. entries.title: Adds new integration [drsassafras/Harman-EASY-Touch-Resolver]
entries.description: A resolver to determine what state your Harman EASY touch pellet stove is in. It is a custom integration with Home Assistant.
entries.readme_excerpt: A Home Assistant integration that works out what a Harman pellet stove is doing by watching how much power it draws. The stove does not report its own state, but each stage of operation (lighting, burning at each heat level, cooling down, idle) has a distinctive power draw. This integration takes a power sensor (in watts), smooths it with a 20 second moving average, maps that average to a state using a profile, and then settles on a final state using per-state timing rules, so brief blips don't cause flapping. It does not talk to the stove. It only reads an existing Home Assistant power sensor

entries.description: Home Assistant coordinator for Mitsubishi MXZ multi-zone mini-splits — fixes the AUTO idle-head deadlock; one explicit shared mode + a single target per room.

Tesla-style Auto for your Mitsubishi multi-split Set a temperature in each room and forget it. entries.readme_excerpt: Teslemetry Bluetooth Commands Bluetooth-only command entities for Tesla vehicles in the Teslemetry integration for Home Assistant. entries.title: Adds new integration [hassanxs/smartsolar-ha]
entries.description: Home Assistant integration for SmartSolar inverter WiFi dongles (Pakistan) — live status, energy, faults and inverter settings
entries.readme_excerpt: SmartSolar for Home Assistant A Home Assistant integration for SmartSolar, the WiFi connectivity dongle sold in Pakistan that brings pure sine wave solar inverters online. It uses the SmartSolar cloud API to read live status, energy usage and faults, and to change inverter settings. This is an unofficial community integration and is not affiliated with SmartSolar. Live status (every 30 s by default): PV, grid, load, battery and inverter readings, plus the inverter mode, charge mode, temperatures and errors. Energy (every 5 min): today's and this month's kWh totals for solar, battery and grid.

entries.title: Adds new integration [infernalK/ha-calendar-share]
entries.description: Home Assistant custom integration: share a calendar as an unauthenticated iCalendar (.ics) subscription feed
entries.readme_excerpt: Share any Home Assistant calendar with your phone, your family or your colleagues, using a simple link. Calendar Share turns a calendar from Home Assistant (school, work, garbage collection, sports club, a Google or CalDAV calendar you already added…) into a private web link. Paste that link into Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook or any app that can "subscribe to a calendar", and the events appear there and stay up to date by themselves. Home Assistant can already show your calendars, but other apps cannot read them: its API requires a login header that calendar apps are unable to send.
entries.name: Calendar Share

entries.title: Adds new integration [seevee/cap_alerts]
entries.description: HA multi-region weather alerts integration: one entity per active weather alert, modeled on CAP fields. Solves the 16KB attribute limit.
entries.readme_excerpt: Weather and hazard alerts for Home Assistant, one entity per active alert. Single-entity alert integrations pack every alert into one attribute blob and run into Home Assistant's 16 KB attribute limit. CAP Alerts gives each alert its own sensor. The state is a normalized severity, the attributes are the fields, and an event fires when an alert is created, updated or removed. The providers are the visible part. The point of the project is the model underneath them: one identity per incident across re-issues, a lifecycle that does not trust feed presence, bounded attributes, and lifecycle events
entries.name: CAP Alerts

entries.title: Adds new integration [yitsewu/taiwan-water]

entries.title: Adds new integration [paolofaz/watch-ble-presence]
entries.description: Home Assistant custom integration that exposes fast, deterministic BLE presence for Apple Watch devices already configured with "Private BLE Device" integration
entries.readme_excerpt: A Home Assistant custom integration for monitoring Apple Watch presence using each Watch's own Identity Resolving Key (IRK). No Private BLE Device integration required. entries.title: Adds new integration [dasimon135/ha-bluesight]
entries.description: See the invisible: read-only Home Assistant integration that surfaces ESPHome Bluetooth-proxy GATT slot allocations and detects deadlocks (core issue #176516), ghost slots, and pairing storms.
entries.readme_excerpt: BlueSight — Home Assistant integration When a Bluetooth device in Home Assistant goes unavailable for no visible reason, this tells you why. Every ESPHome Bluetooth proxy can hold only a handful of Bluetooth connections at once — three, usually. Home Assistant does not show you how many are in use or which device is holding each one, so when they run out, devices simply stop working and nothing says so. BlueSight shows you those connections, names the device holding each one, and flags the three ways they go wrong. What it does not do: anything. BlueSight only reads. It never touches a proxy,

entries.title: Adds new integration [merlijntishauser/ha-usage-score]
entries.description: Home Assistant Usage Score: how much of Home Assistant an instance actually uses, scored across usage, integration diversity, household activity, and hygiene consumed from HAGHS.
entries.readme_excerpt: HAUS — Home Assistant Usage Score Most dashboards tell you what your house is doing. HAUS tells you how much of Home Assistant you are actually using, and what to do next. One sensor scored 0–100 across four pillars, six cards to draw it, and an event to react to. Nothing leaves your instance. HAGHS measures whether an instance is healthy. HAUS measures whether it is being used, and consumes HAGHS for its hygiene pillar rather than competing with it. It works with or without HAGHS installed. Requires Home Assistant 2026.8.0 or newer. HACS → three-dot menu → Custom repositories → add this repos

entries.description: Home Assistant integration that tracks your weight against a planned trajectory
entries.readme_excerpt: A Home Assistant integration that tracks your weight against a planned trajectory: from a start weight to a target weight over a date range, for losing, maintaining or gaining. It reads whatever numeric entity you point it at, from any scale integration you already use, or it takes the weights you type in yourself. Out of that it builds the plan: where you should be today, how far off you are, which way the last few days are trending, and when you arrive at that rate. entries.title: Adds new plugin [ADNPolymerase/ha-printer-card]
entries.description: Home Assistant Lovelace card for printers: an animated sheet while it prints, ink or toner levels, low-cartridge alert and the printer's own status message
entries.readme_excerpt: A Lovelace card for printers: a sheet that really slides out while the machine prints, ink or toner levels drawn as cartridges, the drum and the fuser alongside them, page counters, a low-supply alert and the printer's own status message. No integration is privileged. The state goes through a keyword table rather than one vendor's vocabulary, and the supplies are found by looking at the printer's device rather than at a naming convention, so a Brother drum, a Samsung toner, an Epson maintenance box and a Dell sensor.black all land on the card. Feedback and issues welcome. Four classic machines

entries.title: Adds new integration [cnc-lasercraft/uniali]
entries.description: Home Assistant custom component: UniFi-Client-Aliases mit HA-Friendly-Names synchronisieren — Audit-Card mit Sync pro Zeile, Vendor-Adapter für Shelly und SLZB
entries.readme_excerpt: Keep UniFi client aliases in sync with your Home Assistant friendly names. UniFi aliases are set by hand and drift away from reality. With ~80 Shellys and everything else on the network you get typos, mix-ups and names that were never updated. During diagnosis that actively misleads you — a real example from this network: a Shelly named DGKlima in Home Assistant carried the UniFi alias ShellyMiniQuooker. A custom component plus a Lovelace card: An audit table of every device whose MAC is known both to the HA device registry and to UniFi — three columns: HA friendly name ↔ UniFi alias ↔ device

The integration talks to the doorbell over your own network with the Tuya local protocol: no cloud account, no polling of Tuya's servers, no data leaving the Version 3.0 is a rebuild of how the integration decides what a device is. It talks to XMRig, not to the machine XMRig runs on, so it works against any correctly configured instance — Linux, Windows, macOS, a container, a Raspberry Pi — regardless of how that host was set up. entries.title: Adds new integration [MadMatt34/ha-freebox-caller-id]
entries.description: Détecte en temps réel les appels téléphoniques entrants sur la ligne fixe Freebox
entries.readme_excerpt: Freebox Caller ID - Home Assistant Integration Freebox Caller ID is a custom Home Assistant integration designed to detect incoming calls on your Freebox landline in real-time, without requiring any additional hardware. By default, the Freebox OS API does not send push notifications when a phone rings. However, the Freebox immediately registers incoming calls in its call log (/api/v4/call/log/) upon the very first ring with a duration of 0. This integration performs fast, asynchronous HTTP polling (every 2 seconds by default). Fire a native event (freeboxincomingcall) on the first ring signal.
entries.name: Freebox Caller ID

entries.readme_excerpt: A modern, UI-configured Home Assistant integration for RFLink USB/TCP gateways — covers and sensors only, for now.
